item.title: [LU-21144] Fast unplanned MDT recovery at scale
item.description:
Problem Statement

In large-scale AI/ML and HPC Lustre deployments (3,000+ clients and 10+ DNE MDTs), unplanned MDT recovery (target_recovery_thread()) experiences severe wall-clock stalls and quadratic CPU bottlenecks:

  1. Stage 0 Dead-Client Wait (250-300s stall): struct lsd_client_data in last_rcvd (LR_CLIENT_SIZE = 128) persists lcd_uuid but not the client's struct lnet_nid. If even one client node crashes concurrently with an MDT restart, the recovering MDT cannot actively probe unconnected exports and stalls Stage 1 replay for the full passive obd_recovery_timeout (2.5 * obd_timeout).
  2. Stage 1 Server Request Replay Queue (O(R^2) CPU): target_queue_recovery_request() linearly scans exp_req_replay_queue and obd_req_replay_queue on every out-of-order replay RPC insertion.
  3. Stage 1 Client Committed-Open Replay (O * RTT latency): ptlrpc_replay_next() replays committed open handles on imp_committed_list one RPC at a time (*inflight = 1), even though committed opens (transno < obd_next_recovery_transno) are independent in-memory handle reconstructions on the server.
  4. Stage 1 DNE Cross-MDT Update Recovery (O(U^2) CPU): update_recovery.c allocates replay structures for already-committed batches (ur_batchid <= tdtd_committed_batchid) and performs linear O(U) list scans for batchid and transno lookups.
  5. Stage 2 Server Lock Replay (Single-Threaded Serialization): After Stage 1 completes, all MSG_REQ_REPLAY_DONE lock replay RPCs are queued onto obd_lock_replay_queue and processed serially by the single target_recovery_thread.

Proposed Solution

This improvement addresses all five bottlenecks across a 5-patch series without modifying the Lustre wire protocol or changing the 128-byte last_rcvd client slot layout:

  1. recovery: use rbtree for target req replay queue: Index queued Stage 1 replay requests in an rb_root_cached (obd_req_replay_rbtree) for O(log R) sorted insertion and duplicate transno detection, while keeping O(1) in-flight resent duplicate detection at the head of exp_req_replay_queue. Adds OBD_FAIL_TGT_LEGACY_RECOVERY (0x728) for runtime A/B fallback.
  2. ptlrpc: pipeline client committed-open replays: Pipeline up to 16 concurrent committed-open replay RPCs (PTLRPC_MAX_COMMITTED_REPLAY_INFLIGHT = 16) from imp_committed_list, with monotonic imp_last_replay_transno tracking, error-rewind on timeout, and a strict imp_replay_inflight == 0 barrier before uncommitted imp_replay_list replay.
  3. target: optimize DNE distributed txn recovery: Skip committed DNE update log records (ur_batchid <= tdtd_committed_batchid, including UPDATE_RECORD_CONTINUE chunks) in O(1) time and index active/finished DNE replay items via red-black trees (tdtd_replay_batchid_root, tdtd_replay_transno_root, tdtd_finish_transno_root) for O(log U) lookups.
  4. ldlm: execute Stage 2 lock replays in parallel: Set obd_req_replay_done once Stage 1 finishes so Stage 2 MSG_REQ_REPLAY_DONE lock replay RPCs execute in parallel on PTLRPC worker threads, gated before Stage 3 by an obd_lock_replay_inflight == 0 barrier in check_for_next_lock().
  5. target: probe unconnected client NIDs in recovery: Persist each client export's struct lnet_nid in a sidecar local object (CLIENT_NIDS_OID = 4126UL, "client_nids", indexed by ted_lr_idx) within the same local OSD transaction as last_rcvd. Export LNetPingPeer() and schedule asynchronous workqueue probes for unconnected exports after obd_recovery_probe_delay so unreachable clients are evicted in ~7-10s (enabling VBR) instead of blocking Stage 1 for 250-300s.

Interoperability & Upgrade Compatibility

  • Wire Protocol: Zero RPC or connect-flag changes; old clients interoperate transparently with new servers and vice versa.
  • On-Disk Format: last_rcvd is unchanged. On upgrade, tgt_init() creates client_nids (OID 4126) and tgt_clients_data_init() ignores EOF for pre-upgrade slots until clients reconnect. On downgrade, older releases ignore OID 4126.

Benchmark Results (3,000 Clients x 11 DNE MDTs, 10 Dead Clients)

Recovery Phase Legacy Baseline Fast Recovery Speedup
Stage 0: Dead-Client Eviction Wait (10/3,000 dead) 300.0 s 10.0 s 30.0x
Stage 1: 11-MDT Request Replay Queue (5,990 reqs) 33.40 ms 3.04 ms 11.0x
Stage 1: 11-MDT Committed Opens (352 opens) 36.07 ms (352 RTT) 7.59 ms (22 RTT) 4.8x
Stage 1: 11-MDT Cross-MDT DNE Recovery (4,000 txns) 320.51 ms 3.17 ms 101.2x
Stage 2: 3,000-Client Lock Replay (2,990 locks) 30.96 ms (2,990 waves) 2.15 ms (47 waves) 14.4x
Total Active Replay Execution (Stages 1-2) 420.93 ms 15.94 ms 26.4x
item.summary: Fast unplanned MDT recovery at scale

status.description: The issue is open and ready for the assignee to start work on it.

comments.comment: mironikolov are you working on a patch to implement your proposed solution?
Yes I am working on a patch with the proposed solution

struct lsd_client_data in last_rcvd (LR_CLIENT_SIZE = 128) persists lcd_uuid but not the client's struct lnet_nid

We have implemented the same for the maintenance mode in LU-20359, for basically the same reason - to allow the server to contact clients after recovery. I can provide a patch with the on-disk format next week.
